slides.headline: When flexibility isn't the thing to train
slides.sub: Why control matters more than range for very bendy bodies.

slides.title: Bendy isn't the same as strong
slides.body: Some people's joints move further than average. That isn't a problem on its own, but it can mean muscles work harder to control the range, which may lead to fatigue or aches.

slides.title: Skip the end-range stretches
slides.body: Many flexible people love sinking into deep stretches. In Pilates, the aim is to work in the middle of your range with control, rather than hanging on your joints at the end.

slides.title: Slow down and feel it
slides.body: Slower movements, lighter springs and smaller ranges help you feel which muscles are working. It can feel oddly harder than big, flowing moves, and that's usually a good sign.

slides.title: Build strength gradually
slides.body: Add load bit by bit with reformer springs, bands and body weight. Research suggests strength training is a helpful part of managing symptoms for many people with hypermobility.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: If joints often feel like they partly slip out, you have widespread pain, or you're unusually fatigued, it's worth chatting with your GP or physio for a proper assessment.

slides.headline: Flexible? Let's build control
slides.body: Our Pilates team assesses how you move and builds a program focused on control and strength, at a pace that suits you. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Always the most flexible person in the class? Your Pilates goals might look a little different.

Some people's joints move further than average. That isn't a problem on its own, but muscles may need to work harder to control the range, which can lead to fatigue or aches.

Instead of sinking into deep stretches, work in the middle of your range with control. Slow down, use lighter springs and smaller movements, and build strength gradually. Research suggests strength training is a helpful part of managing symptoms for many people with hypermobility.

If joints often feel like they partly slip out, or you have widespread pain or unusual fatigue, chat with your GP or physio.

story.headline: Very flexible? Train control
story.body: Work mid-range, slow down, use lighter springs and build strength gradually. Range isn't the goal.
